thread.title: ASIA MARKETS: Asian Stock Markets Recover, Led By Japan And Hong Kong

author: morningstar.com
title: ASIA MARKETS: Asian Stock Markets Recover, Led By Japan And Hong Kong
text:
By Dow Jones Newswire
Nikkei flips to positive for the year
Asian stock markets bounced back Thursday, led by strong gains in Japan and Hong Kong, as the U.S. offered to renew trade talks with China (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/us-offers-renewed-trade-talks-with-china-to-avert-new-tariffs-2018-09-12).
After falling for seven of the past nine sessions, Japan's Nikkei was up nearly 1% as the index pushed back into positive territory for 2018. SoftBank (9984.TO) was up some 4.7%, and export-reliant companies such as Toyota (7203.TO) and Honda (HMC) were up nearly 2%.
Hong Kong stocks, down for six straight days, roared back to life, with the Hang Seng Index up 2.5%. Mainland heavyweights including Tencent (0700.HK) , China Construction Bank (0939.HK) and Ping An (2318.HK) were strong while Geely (0175.HK) rebounded more than 8% and beaten-down Macau casinos stocks climbed. But drugmakers remained under pressure on looming price cuts, with Sino Biopharma (1177.HK) and CSPC (1093.HK) both lower.
Trade hopes helped Chinese stocks rise, with the Shanghai Composite up 1.1% after three straight declines while the Shenzhen Composite gained 0.7%.
Korea's Kospi , which came into today's trading down 7.5% for the year, was up 0.1%, with Samsung (005930.SE) down 1.1%. Taiwan's Taiex was about flat, though chip maker Taiwan Semiconductor (2330.TW) fell after the unveiling of the new iPhones, which feature advanced A12 Bionic chips it produced with partner Apple Inc. (AAPL)
Australia's ASX 200 was one of the few laggards on the day, down over 0.7%. New Zealand gained nearly 0.6%. Benchmarks in Singapore , Malaysia and Indonesia rose.
